review.publication: Local database and working tree only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Dictionary reconciliation: measurement instruments, their functions and targets, unit families, all seven SI base-unit names, and selected everyday units.

dictionary_comparison.caveat: String matches are candidates, not verified sense alignments. No exact English candidate does not establish that a concept is absent; Russian labels, aliases and graph context require review.

review.attribution: Uses reviewed and adapted lexical data from Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton University WordNet. OEWN additions are licensed CC BY 4.0; the Princeton notice is reproduced in the Q11 report. Unit classifications are independently checked against the BIPM SI Brochure (CC BY 4.0). Russian labels, selection, scope restrictions and graph mappings are adaptations; no endorsement is implied.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use the existing Everyday context U1. Existing home contexts are preserved; U2 remains empty.
review.method: Full normalized English lemma comparison generates candidates only. Each selected meaning is checked against all existing names and RU/EN aliases, its existing parents, and dictionary sense definitions. Synsets and synonyms are selected manually. Productive measurement phrases are marked as composed meanings supported by instrument definitions, not invented dictionary entries.

review.limits: This is the first reviewed dictionary batch, not a complete semantic comparison of 107519 synsets. Exact English mismatches are not absence counts. No relation grammar changes or automatic WordNet hypernym, antonym, or synonym import. Unit conversion factors are review metadata only: genus is not a scale-conversion relation. No obsolete SI definitions, unqualified ton, impedance/resistivity aliases for resistance, or measuring-system synonym for an individual instrument. Unit symbols are selected explicitly and are not generated by case folding. No application test suites.
